title: The most terrifying sentence Jesus ever said was not about flames.
paragraphs: The most terrifying sentence Jesus ever said was not about flames.
Not about outer darkness.
Not about weeping and gnashing of teeth.
It was seven words that almost nobody talks about deeply enough.
“Ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν, οὐκ οἶδα ὑμᾶς.”
“Amen, I tell you… I do not know you.”
— Matthew 25:12
Not “you never went to church.”
Not “you never posted Bible verses.”
Not “you weren’t religious enough.”
“I do not know you.”
And if that sentence does not shake something inside your soul… you may not understand what Jesus was actually saying.
Because in Scripture, to be “known” by God was never casual recognition.
The Greek word Jesus used here is “οἶδα” (oida).

It means:
to truly know,
to recognize intimately,
to perceive deeply,
to be personally connected with.

This was not Jesus saying,
“I forgot your name.”

This was Jesus saying,
“You stood near Me… but never belonged to Me.”
That is horrifying.
Because it means proximity to Christianity is not the same as intimacy with Christ.
You can sing worship songs and still be spiritually unknown.
You can quote Scripture and still be spiritually unknown.
You can build an online ministry and still be spiritually unknown.

You can preach sermons and still hear:
“I never knew you.”
The terrifying part is that many people Jesus warned were completely convinced they were safe.
“Κύριε, κύριε…”
“Lord, Lord…”
Matthew 7:22
Notice that.
They called Him Lord.

Not atheist.
Not pagan.
Not unbeliever.
Religious people.
Church people.
People who thought they were fine.
And Jesus says something so emotionally devastating that it almost feels unbearable to read honestly.
“Καὶ τότε ὁμολογήσω αὐτοῖς ὅτι· Οὐδέποτε ἔγνων ὑμᾶς.”
“And then I will declare to them: I never knew you.”
— Matthew 7:23
The word “ἔγνων” (egnōn) comes from “γινώσκω” (ginōskō).
This is even deeper than intellectual awareness.

It speaks of relational knowing.
Experiential knowing.
Covenantal intimacy.
The same word used for deep personal union.
Jesus was not exposing weak church attendance.
He was exposing counterfeit intimacy.
And suddenly the conversation becomes personal.
Because many people today know Christian culture better than they know Christ Himself.

They know worship trends.
Podcast theology.
Denominational arguments.
TikTok sermons.
Motivational Christianity.
But they do not know Jesus in secret.

No surrender.
No repentance.
No hidden prayer life.
No real obedience when nobody is watching.
Only performance.
Only appearance.
Only carefully edited spirituality.
And the scariest part?
It can fool everyone around you.
But not Him.
In Revelation 3:1, Jesus speaks to the church in Sardis with another terrifying statement:
“ὄνομα ἔχεις ὅτι ζῇς, καὶ νεκρὸς εἶ.”
“You have a reputation for being alive, but you are dead.”
Dead people can still look religious.
That should terrify every one of us.
Because Christianity was never meant to be cosmetic.
The Hebrew understanding of knowing God was always relational.

In Hebrew, the word “יָדַע” (yada) means:
to know intimately,
to experience personally,
to walk closely with.
Genesis says Adam “knew” Eve.
Not information.
Intimacy.
Connection.
Union.
So when Scripture speaks of knowing God, it is not talking about memorizing verses while your heart remains distant.
It is talking about surrender.
Transformation.
Communion.
Walking with Him when nobody applauds you.
There are people who know theology but do not know Jesus.
And there are broken people with trembling prayers that heaven recognizes instantly.
That is why the tax collector in Luke 18 went home justified while the proud religious man did not.
One performed.
One surrendered.
One impressed people.
One cried for mercy.
And heaven responded to the honest sinner.
This is where the article becomes uncomfortable.
Because some people reading this have mastered appearing Christian while secretly being exhausted from pretending.
You post strength while privately collapsing.
You post faith while privately numb.
You know how to sound spiritual while your prayer life has gone silent.

And deep down, there is this quiet fear:
“What if I have been near Jesus… without truly knowing Him?”
Listen carefully.
Conviction is not condemnation.
If your heart is being pierced right now, that is not proof God abandoned you.
It may be proof He is calling you back before your heart hardens completely.
Because the same Jesus who warned with terrifying honesty also invited with terrifying mercy.
In John 10:14, Jesus says:
“ἐγώ εἰμι ὁ ποιμὴν ὁ καλός, καὶ γινώσκω τὰ ἐμά.”
“I am the Good Shepherd. I know My own.”
He knows His sheep.
Not perfectly polished sheep.
Not flawless sheep.
His sheep.

The struggling.
The weary.
The repentant.
The honest.
The broken who still run toward Him instead of away from Him.
That is the difference.
Not perfection.
Relationship.
Real repentance is not pretending you never failed.
It is refusing to hide from God after you fail.
Peter denied Jesus three times.
Judas betrayed Jesus once.
One ran back in repentance.
One ran away in despair.
The difference was not the size of the sin.
The difference was surrender.
And maybe that is why this subject cuts so deeply.
Because many people fear hell while still avoiding intimacy with Christ.
But eternal life itself was never merely about escaping punishment.
Jesus defined eternal life personally.
“αὕτη δέ ἐστιν ἡ αἰώνιος ζωή, ἵνα γινώσκωσίν σε…”
“And this is eternal life: that they may know You…”
— John 17:3
Eternal life begins with knowing Him now.
Not someday.
Now.
Not religious performance.
Relationship.
Not image management.
Surrender.
Not public Christianity with private rebellion.
Real communion with Christ.
And maybe somebody reading this needed to hear this today:
God is not asking you to become impressive.
He is asking you to become honest.
The enemy loves fake perfection because fake perfection never seeks healing.

But broken honesty?
That is where transformation begins.
Some of you have spent years trying to look spiritually alive while quietly dying inside.
Jesus never asked for your performance.
He asked for your heart.

And the terrifying sentence:
“I never knew you”
was never meant to drive repentant people away from Him.
It was meant to wake up those hiding behind religious masks before it is too late.
So stop pretending.
Stop performing.
Stop curating holiness while secretly starving spiritually.
Run back to Christ honestly.
Cry honestly.
Pray honestly.
Repent honestly.
Because the greatest tragedy would not be failing publicly.
The greatest tragedy would be standing before Jesus after spending your whole life pretending to know Him… only to discover you never truly surrendered to Him at all.
And maybe that is why this sentence is more terrifying than descriptions of hell itself.
Because separation from Christ was always the real horror.
Not flames.
Not darkness.

Him saying:
“You wanted religion without relationship.
You wanted salvation without surrender.
You wanted My benefits without Me.”
And suddenly every fake mask becomes meaningless forever.
Somebody else reading your confession may realize they are not alone tonight.
One day, every performance will die… but your relationship with Jesus Christ will remain forever.
